title: Lone pairs close the bond angle
caption: Methane, ammonia and water all have four electron pairs arranged tetrahedrally. Lone pairs repel more strongly than bonding pairs, so each lone pair squeezes the bond angle by about 2.5°: 109.5° in CH₄, 107° in NH₃, 104.5° in H₂O.
alt: CH₄ tetrahedral at 109.5°, NH₃ trigonal pyramidal at 107° with one lone pair, H₂O bent at 104.5° with two lone pairs.
description: NH₃: three bonding pairs and one lone pair, trigonal pyramidal, 107°.
H₂O: two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, bent, 104.5°.
